title: refactor: cleanups
desiredOutcome: The remaining honesty debts are paid: cost_bands parity is asserted from a shared fixture instead of a comment’s presence, audit-status imports _fmt directly, audit-doctor uses _loader, and hooks/_config gains section headers without gaining imports.

tasks.title: cost_bands parity: shared boundary fixture, both sides assert it
tasks.description: usage_ledger.cost_bands() is hand-mirrored in the panel JS, kept honest only by a selftest that checks the COMMENT is still present. Replace with a shared boundary fixture (band edges as data) asserted from usage_ledger’s selftest and from the panel selftest against the JS source — the logic must agree, not the prose.

add: band-boundary fixture asserted from both sides; comment-presence pin retired

outcome.technical: usage_ledger.COST_BAND_PARAMS (gate 5, percentiles 50/90) is the single source cost_bands() reads from; panel-server injects it into panel.js via a __COST_BAND_PARAMS__ placeholder (json.dumps of the module constant through the existing loader path) and uBandInfo() reads it instead of restating literals. The comment-presence pin is retired for three logic pins (placeholder-once, JS-reads-placeholder, assembled-carries-the-constant) plus two ledger-side cases; four mutation proofs red by name. usage_ledger 127/127, panel-server 240/240 (238 + 3 new - 1 retired).
outcome.descriptive: The cost bands have one definition, injected where the browser needs it, and the check that used to prove a comment now proves the logic.

tasks.title: audit-status: sectioning + direct _fmt import
tasks.description: Internal section headers; import _fmt directly and retire the audit-usage fmt indirection once nothing external loads it.

outcome.technical: audit-status gains house-style section headers and imports _fmt directly (the one formatter since P10.6), dropping the audit-usage indirection for the fmt helpers; audit-usage's aliases stay for other consumers. 120/120 and 59/59 hold; sweep and lint green.
outcome.descriptive: audit-status reads its numbers from the module that owns them and is navigable by section.
